archival_prior.era_caveat: PRE-L8/L9 ENGINE. This table shows the exact pathologies L8 (default-seed DSBPL restart) and L9 (widened Ep caps + BOUND_CAPPED diagnosis) were written to fix - see bound_pathologies below. Every count here is therefore a LOWER LIMIT on curvature/two-break content and an UPPER-uncertainty on the BB content.

union_rule_counts.rule_as_specified: a block counts if LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 AND BANDBB_KT > 1.05, and/or LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 AND CPLBB_KT > 1.05 - BOTH nested tests evaluated, reported as union and intersection separately (never as 'the' dAIC; T8 baseline rule)
union_rule_counts.cpl_bb_test_fires: 3 blocks - 3, 4, 5 (block 6 misses at LRT = 9.0948, just under the 9.2 threshold)
union_rule_counts.marginal_block_disclosed: BLOCK 6 is the whole difference between union and intersection: LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 9.4698 (fires) vs LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 9.0948 (misses) - a 0.375 spread straddling the threshold. Its BIC winner is CPL while its AIC winner is CPL+BB. Treat as UNDECIDED, not as a detection.
union_rule_counts.block_minus1_integrated: LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 47.5698 with CPLBB_KT = 55.155 keV fires the CPL+BB test, but (a) LRT_BANDBB_BAND is NaN because BAND_STATUS = FAIL on this row, so the Band pairing could not be evaluated at all, and (b) CPLBB_VALID = False. The integrated row is NOT counted in either number above and must not be quoted.

kt_values_keV.consistency_note: in every firing block the Band+BB and CPL+BB temperatures agree to <0.3% - the temperature is NOT an artifact of which continuum it rides on, which is the one internal check available here (T7).
kt_values_keV.L25_caution: kT ~ 2.2-3.6 keV puts the BB nuFnu peak at ~3.92 kT = 9-14 keV - AT the NaI low-energy threshold (8 keV). This is a low-energy-EDGE component, exactly the class L25 warns about (xb ~ 3.92 kT, r = 0.87) and exactly the band the Earth-limb hazard (P-E) would corrupt. It must NOT be called a photosphere on these numbers.

two_break_content.impossible_negatives: 6 of 9 blocks (-1, 0, 3, 4, 5, 6) return a NEGATIVE nested LRT for DSBPL vs SBPL. DSBPL contains SBPL, so a negative nested LRT is arithmetically impossible and diagnoses OPTIMIZER FAILURE, not physics. This is the L8 default-seed DSBPL pathology, manifest on six blocks.

bound_pathologies.BAND_ALPHA railed at -1.9: blocks 3 (-1.8999999994), 4 (-1.8999999996), 5 (-1.8999999771) - the low-energy index sits ON its hard bound in all three BB-firing blocks. An alpha pinned at a bound and an additive BB compete for the same low-energy curvature; this ALONE makes the archival BB significances untrustworthy as magnitudes.
bound_pathologies.CPL_XC at or near the 50 keV-to-50 MeV c: block 0 (49997.0), block 5 (49988.6); also very large in blocks 2 (33128), -1 (23394), 4 (13188), 3 (6267). A CPL whose cutoff runs to the cap IS a power law - directly consistent with the published PL-best verdict.
bound_pathologies.VALID flags mostly False: e.g. block 4 and 5 have only CPLBB_VALID = True of six models; block 0 only SBPL. The adequacy/validity gate was already rejecting most of the ladder.

external_frame.internal_catalog_inconsistency_recorded_: The catalog's own two fluence numbers do not line up: the duration-interval fluence is 1.0775e-05 erg/cm2 (10-1000 keV, NaI 4+5, [+0.560,+23.344] s) while the model-integrated PL energy fluence is 1.2552e-05 erg/cm2 over the SHORTER flnc window [-1.024,+16.384] s with n4+n5+b0 - 17% LARGER over ~70% of the duration. Different detector sets, different estimators (counts-based vs model-integrated), possibly different band handling. Per T5/L26 this is RECORDED, not silently resolved, and BOTH must be frame-aligned before any fluence diff.

predictions: P-A (curvature is UNCONSTRAINED; external-frame, falsifiable): every published curved model leaves the break unconstrained - CPL Ep = 814 +/- 365 keV (2.2 sigma), Band Ep = 757 +/- 710 (1.1 sigma), SBPL Ebreak = 2239 +/- 20084 (0.1 sigma) - while a bare PL with index -1.876 +/- 0.013 is declared best. PREDICT: in AT LEAST HALF our blocks the curvature parameter (Band Ep / CPL xc / SBPL Ebreak) is either unconstrained (fractional error >= 50%) or contacts a fit bound, i.e. the L9 BOUND_CAPPED diagnosis fires in >= 4 of 8 blocks. FALSIFIED if >= 50% of blocks return a curvature energy to better than 30% fractional error with no bound contact.

P-A2 (low-energy index and the -1.9 bound; falsifiable, and it targets an UNPUBLISHED decision): published alpha = -1.85033 +/- 0.02246 (Band, integrated) and PL index = -1.876 +/- 0.013 - a soft spectrum far below the synchrotron line of death. PREDICT our window-integrated low-energy index lands in [-2.10, -1.60]. SEPARATELY PREDICT, from the archival prior's BAND_ALPHA sitting exactly on its -1.9 hard bound in all three BB-firing blocks: after the L9 widening, alpha in blocks 3-5 moves OFF the bound to a value softer than -1.9, and the Band+BB LRT in those blocks DROPS relative to the archival 44.2/37.9/42.5. FALSIFIED if alpha still rails at -1.9 post-L9, or if the Band+BB LRTs are unchanged to within 10%.

P-B (the BB / union rule - the headline, falsifiable): NO blackbody claim exists anywhere in this burst's literature, and the GBM catalog never tested an additive component (T7: its 4-model menu has none), so its 'PL is best' is silent about a BB rather than evidence against one. The archival prior fires the union rule in 4 of 8 blocks (3,4,5,6) and the intersection in 3 (3,4,5), t = 2.60-10.64 s, with kT = 2.24-3.55 keV agreeing between the Band+BB and CPL+BB pairings to <0.3%. PREDICT the re-run reproduces a union-rule detection in AT LEAST blocks 3, 4 and 5, with kT staying inside [1.5, 5.0] keV. FALSIFIED if the union rule fires in zero blocks, if kT leaves that range in a reproducing block, or if the count rises above 6 of 8. WHICHEVER WAY IT LANDS THIS IS AN UNPUBLISHED-DECISION result to be scored against the expert band, NOT a literature reconciliation - there is nothing published to reconcile against.

P-B2 (the BB is a low-energy-EDGE feature and must be adjudicated as one; procedural, falsifiable): kT ~ 2.2-3.6 keV puts the nuFnu peak at 3.92 kT = 9-14 keV, i.e. within ~1.5 keV of the NaI 8 keV threshold. PREDICT the BB's inferred flux fraction is strongly covariant with the low-energy index (|rho| > 0.7 between kT/F_BB and alpha across blocks) and that the component therefore CANNOT be promoted to a photosphere on this burst's data. FALSIFIED if the BB survives with the continuum index free and unrailed AND with a demonstrated per-NaI residual coherence (L28). CRITICAL LIMITATION TO CARRY: L28 coherence has almost NO leverage here - there are only TWO NaIs, and one (n5, 56.45 deg) is outside the <=50 deg preference. A two-detector coherence test is nearly vacuous, so the usual acquittal route for a low-energy component is unavailable on this burst. Say so in the write-up rather than quietly running L28 and reporting a pass.

P-C (two-break; falsifiable, plus an engine-hardening prediction): no two-break claim is published, and the catalog's own one-break SBPL leaves Ebreak = 2239 +/- 20084 keV, i.e. undetermined. PREDICT DSBPL does NOT win by dAIC >= 10 in ANY block. SEPARATELY PREDICT, from the archival prior's SIX impossible negative nested LRTs (DSBPL vs SBPL: -17.70, -3.49, -4.16, -12.60, -9.57, -0.98 in blocks -1,0,3,4,5,6): after the L8 default-seed DSBPL restart hardening, ZERO blocks return a negative nested DSBPL-SBPL LRT. FALSIFIED if any negative nested LRT survives L8, or if DSBPL wins by dAIC >= 10 anywhere - the latter would be a genuine unpublished discovery candidate and must clear the L8 seed-artifact check FIRST.

P-D (temporal; external-frame, falsifiable): Maccary+2025 give FWHM_min = 8.43 (-2.18/+2.94) s from MEPSA with Npeaks = 1, against T90 = 22.78 s - the narrowest structure is more than a third of the burst. PREDICT our block decomposition of [-2,+23] s yields a SINGLE dominant pulse (no second significant peak) resolved into >= 4 blocks, and that our MVT-equivalent lands in [2, 15] s. FALSIFIED by a multi-peak decomposition, by fewer than 4 blocks, or by an MVT < 1 s. NOTE the estimator trap (T3): Maccary's FWHM_min, Golkhou's wavelet dt_min and MEPSA's dt_det are three DIFFERENT quantities - do not diff across them.

P-E (EARTH-LIMB GEOMETRY - the dominant hazard on this burst; falsifiable, NAMED ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS): computed here from glg_poshist_all_150630_v01.fit at the GBM catalog position and verified with two independent primitives (astropy SkyCoord.separation and the project's own _angular_distance; spacecraft latitude reproduces poshist SC_LAT exactly), the source CROSSED THE EARTH'S GEOMETRIC LIMB AT T0-5.2 s and sits only 0.16-1.72 deg above it across the entire stamped window. Line-of-sight tangent height by archival block: b0 13.1 km, b1 18.9, b2 18.9, b3 24.7, b4 33.2, b5 38.9, b6 47.4, b7 61.3 km - rising monotonically. A systematic whose strength falls monotonically across exactly our source window can mimic BOTH a FRED rise and a hard-to-soft evolution, and it bites hardest below ~50 keV, which is precisely where the P-B blackbody lives. NOTE THE COINCIDENCE THAT MUST BE TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: the union rule fires in blocks 3-6 (tangent height 24.7-47.4 km, the partial-transmission regime) and NOT in blocks 0-2 (13-19 km) or block 7 (61 km). PREDICT this is a brightness coincidence, not a geometry effect: kT does NOT correlate with tangent height across the firing blocks. FALSIFIED - i.e. the atmosphere is CONVICTED and the BB must be withdrawn - if |Spearman rho(kT, tangent height)| > 0.8 at p < 0.05 across blocks 0-7, OR if the fitted low-energy index hardens monotonically with tangent height at fixed flux. COUNTER-EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND, recorded for balance: von Kienlin+2020 Table 5 leaves the f_Fermi flag BLANK for this burst although 171 rows in that table carry a flag and footnote 'c' reads 'Partial earth occultation is likely; durations are lower limits' - the GBM team positively judged no occultation caveat applies; and GBM plainly recorded a 24 ph/cm2/s pulse that a 13 km tangent height could not transmit. The most economical reconciliation is that THE TRUE POSITION IS SEVERAL DEGREES FURTHER FROM THE LIMB THAN THE CATALOG POSITION (systematic ~3-4 deg vs the quoted 1.46 deg statistical) - itself a falsifiable inference, testable if the Konus-Wind / INTEGRAL SPI-ACS / Mars Observer detections (vK+2020 'Other' = K, IA, Mo) are ever triangulated. DO NOT resolve this inside the fit; carry it as a disclosed alternative.

P-F (background validity under the limb geometry; falsifiable): the source is BELOW the geometric limb for the ENTIRE pre-burst background window (tangent height -282 km at -91 s, -19 km at -11 s) and well above it for the whole post window (+136 km at +45 s, +314 km at +124 s). The polynomial therefore interpolates across a real, monotonic Earth-albedo gradient rather than across a flat baseline. PREDICT the fitted background shows NO coherent one-sided residual run at either inner edge. FALSIFIED if a coherent excess or deficit appears in the last ~10 s of any pre-window or the first ~10 s of any post-window, in which case the inner edges must be revisited before any block-level flux - and especially any BB flux fraction - is quoted. Note n5's windows were human-ADJUSTED away from the n4/b0 values (pre [-74.298,-15.298], post [34.702,120.702]), so n5 samples a slightly different stretch of that gradient than n4 and b0: check the three separately, not as one.

P-G (2-NaI geometry and D5 blockage; falsifiable): the detector set is FORCED - n4 at 23.05 deg, n5 at 56.45 deg, next-nearest n3 at 67.19 deg - so n5 sits outside the <=50 deg NaI preference with no substitute available. PREDICT the EAC cross-normalisation of n5 against the n4 reference stays inside [0.80, 1.20] and does not rail at a bound in more than 25% of fits. FALSIFIED if n5 rails low (<=0.9 systematically, the D5 blockage signature) or rails at a bound in a majority of fits - which would simultaneously convict the detector AND gut P-B, since with only two NaIs there is no third detector to arbitrate. Whatever the outcome, the with/without pair is RETAINED and no detector is dropped from production (the data-dropping hierarchy: quality exclusion only, through the documented gate).

P-H (component coverage and fluence frames; procedural, falsifiable): our stamped window [-2.0,+23.0] s is a strict SUPERSET of the catalog's fluence-spectrum window [-1.024,+16.384] s (which covers only ~70% of T90 and stops 7 s before T95), and is essentially co-extensive with T90 = [+0.560,+23.344] s. PREDICT our window-integrated 10-1000 keV energy fluence exceeds the catalog's flnc-window PL value of 1.2552e-05 erg/cm2. FALSIFIED if ours comes out lower - which would indicate a normalisation or band-handling difference rather than a coverage difference, and would have to be chased before any energetics statement. ALSO PREDICT that any 'our T90 disagrees with the catalog' statement is an artifact: re-align (i) the band (theirs 50-300 keV, ours 8 keV-40 MeV, with T90 ~ E^-0.20 per Qin+2013), (ii) the detector set (theirs NaI 4+5 only for durations, n4+n5+b0 for spectra), and (iii) the estimator, BEFORE calling anything a discrepancy. And carry forward the catalog's OWN unresolved 17% fluence inconsistency (1.0775e-05 duration-interval vs 1.2552e-05 model-integrated over a shorter window) as a systematic floor on any fluence comparison.
